title: Characterize which graphs admit robustly acyclic orientations

problemStatement.plain: Characterize which graphs admit robustly acyclic orientations - orientations that remain acyclic after any single edge reversal. Connected to the Pretzel-Brightwell cover graph characterization.
whyMatters: Connects graph orientation theory to partial order theory
Resolves an open question from Erdős problem #1006 about high-girth graph orientations

proven: Empty graphs admit robustly acyclic orientations
Bipartite graphs admit robustly acyclic orientations
Cover graphs of posets admit robustly acyclic orientations (via rank function)
Rank function on finite partial orders is strictly monotone
knownResults.goal: Prove the constructive direction of the cover graph characterization

currentState.focus: Proved cover_graph_admits_robust by constructing poset rank function
currentState.activeApproach: Rank function counting strictly smaller elements

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETED: All sorries in cover_graph_admits_robust resolved. File has 6 proved theorems, 3 axiomatized deep results, 0 sorries.
builtItems: posetRank : V → ℕ (rank function counting strictly smaller elements)
posetRank_strictMono : a < b → posetRank a < posetRank b
insights: The rank function rank(a) = |{x : x < a}| is strictly monotone on any finite partial order
Both acyclicity and no-dependent-arcs follow from the same rank function
The cover orientation (u → v when u ⋖ v) gives a robustly acyclic orientation because the rank function works for all arcs simultaneously

approaches.name: Poset rank function
approaches.description: Define rank(a) = |{x ∈ V : x < a}| and show it witnesses both acyclicity and independence of all arcs
